label: The advisor's compiled graph metadata embeds the example domains as sk-code routing signals: $.signals.sk-code[2] = webflow; [42] obsidian plugin; [43] obsidian plugin source; [45] obsidian plugin design system; [77] obsidian plugin conventions. One sk-code node (skill_count 14, families.sk-code: [sk-code]); surface packets are not graph nodes.

The advisor's hardcoded lexical lane boosts sk-code on 'obsidian plugin' (comment: sk-code declares that exact phrase and was losing to a bare-token overlap by 0.004); the lane's sk-code array has no webflow token.

webflow cms is disambiguated away from sk-code as MCP-tooling vocabulary: explicit.ts:131 anchors 'webflow cms' to mcp-code-mode (+1.5) and sk-code (-0.5); fusion.ts:598-602 toolchain regex adds bonus/penalty; skill_advisor.py:2031 maps 'webflow cms' to mcp-code-mode (2.2).

The advisor has zero references to sk-code-obsidian/sk-code-webflow ids (case-insensitive grep over the whole advisor tree: no matches). Surfaces are advisor-invisible by design ('metadata' is the default routing class for every surface packet). Deleting the two packets cannot break advisor identity or graph nodes.

The advisor's own surfaceHint is a pass-through, not a ranker: advisor_recommend accepts options.surfaceHint (bounded <=64 chars) and forwards it to compiled-route.cjs as its own --surface-hint argv pair; no hint means the flag is omitted.

Advisor regression/holdout corpora name webflow but assert mcp-code-mode: case P1-MCP-002 'fetch webflow cms collection' expects mcp-code-mode in both fixtures/skill-advisor-regression-cases.jsonl:14 and routing-accuracy/holdout-prompts.jsonl:32. No case asserts an sk-code surface route.

Doctor 5k-canary couples routerSignals to the static fixture: every routerSignals mode must be the expected route of a case in the hub's canary fixture (canaryDrift :1232-1241, reported :1284-1285); a hub without a fixture dir gets INFO 'leg not applicable' (:1272-1274). Deleting a surface forces coordinated edits of hub-router.json routerSignals and the canary fixture, or the doctor fails 5k-canary.

Doctor 5k also carries alias and packet legs (:1184-1230) and a WARN-only hub list VOCABULARY_PARITY_WARN_ONLY (mcp-tooling/sk-design/sk-doc/system-deep-loop at :1291). sk-code is not on it, so sk-code vocabulary drift fails hard.

The root README instructs replacement but keeps all three as shipped: :800 'Three ready surfaces: WEBFLOW, OPENCODE, OBSIDIAN'; :1384 'Replace the shipped Webflow + OpenCode + Obsidian surfaces with your own'; :1447 'Replace the surface packets (sk-code-webflow/, sk-code-opencode/, sk-code-obsidian/) with packets for your stack'. It never says the doctor assumes the two examples are gone, and it presents OpenCode as replaceable like the others.
.skilled/README.md does not exist (fs.existsSync false); the dispatch-named path is not in the tree. The external-facing doc is the root README.md (1601 lines).

Git hooks check sk-code but not the surfaces: both pre-commit copies gate comment hygiene via sk-code-quality/scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh (SOURCE_ROOT-relative) and name no surface packet; a deleted surface cannot break them.

Doctor runtime-mirror checks point into the sk-code hub: doctor-runtime-mirrors.yaml:68-100 requires sk-code-quality/scripts/check-dist-staleness.sh on claude/cursor/codex SessionStart hooks. It targets sk-code-quality, so deleting the two surface packets leaves it intact.

The doctor carries a dedicated parent-skill/router/update command set (doctor-parent-skill.yaml, doctor-router-reach.yaml, doctor-update-align.yaml); parent-skill-check.cjs (2010 lines, invariants 1a-5k) is the per-hub auditor, DEFAULT_TARGET .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop (:130); the audited hub list is not established from this read.
The doctor's MCP asset names the two domains: mcp-mutation-class-manifest.yaml has obsidian|webflow matches at lines 80, 81, 82, 87 - MCP tooling mutation classes, not sk-code surfaces.
